subject: Decision log: batching/caching/quantization choices for NimbusAI onboarding
messages:
From: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@nimbus.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsiao <tom@Nimbus.ai>
Date: 2025-06-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: cost/perf decisions we need for POC

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. The POC is greenlit by our infra team; before we spin up dedicated capacity we need to lock a small set of implementation choices so we can size and budget accurately. High level asks:

- Recommended batching sizes and expected latency at 95p for short chat queries (avg 40–80 tokens).
- Whether we should enable prefix/KV prefetching for our LLM workload (customer support use case).
- Quantization recommendations — we currently prefer 8-bit but are open to 4-bit if quality holds.
- Any routing rules that would help keep our costs predictable (e.g., route large-batch jobs to cheaper pool).

I've attached a small sample trace and our token distribution. Can someone from your side propose a short decision log with concrete options?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Ruiz
Head of ML Ops, NimbusAI
[Attachment: nimbus_prefetch_profile_v1.csv]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-22T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: cost/perf decisions we need for POC

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the sample traces, that helps. I'm looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Monica (implementation PM) so we can put a short decision log together and call out tradeoffs. High-level proposals from my side:

1) Batching: Start with dynamic batching with a soft cap at 8 requests per batch for chat-style queries (target 60–80 ms added queuing at 95p on A100-class instances). We can tune to 4–6 if latency is the primary constraint.

2) KV prefetching: Recommend enabling KV prefetch for conversations where the prompt includes prior turns >256 tokens. That should reduce decode latency by ~15–25% for warm sessions.

3) Quantization: Recommend shipping a 4-bit LLM variant for non-critical paths (low-latency, high-throughput routes) after quality validation. Start POC on 8-bit baseline and run a blind eval on a 2k-sample prompt set.

4) Routing: Suggest a two-tier routing policy: 
- Latency-first route to a small pool (higher-cost) for interactive sessions flagged as "live-support".
- Cost-first route (4-bit or larger batching) for bulk post-processing jobs.

I'll prepare a short decision log template and a mutual action plan. Monica / Marissa — can you confirm which operational constraints we should preserve in the MAP (maintenance windows, data-retention, audit requirements)?

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Samantha Ruiz <samantha@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-23T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: cost/perf decisions we need for POC

Thanks — adding a couple of operational items for the MAP:

- Audit & logs: Nimbus asked for request/response retention of 30 days for initial POC; we can hold full payloads but recommend token redaction for PII.
- Maintenance windows: mark weekly patch windows (Tue 0300–0400 UTC) where we may fail fastover to hosted fallback.
- Rollout cadence: plan three stages — baseline (8-bit, no prefetch), staged (enable prefetch + small batching), experiment (4-bit variant behind canary).

Action items I volunteered for: compile the MAP doc and include expected cost delta estimates for each stage. I'll attach a short quant recommendation summary for Nimbus to review.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: quant-recommendation-summary.pdf]
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Samantha Ruiz <samantha@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-24T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: cost/perf decisions we need for POC

Quick implementation questions from infra:

- What is Nimbus's expected concurrency (RPS) for live support vs async processing? We need that to size the reserved pool and to recommend batch timers.
- For KV prefetching: do you have a stable user-id/session token we can key on, or do we need a sticky-routing option?
- For quality validation on 4-bit: can Nimbus provide a 2k-sample labelled set or do you want Redwood to run an automated A/B with human raters?

Tentative internal timeline: if we get concurrency and sample set by Tue 6/30, we can ship baseline (8-bit, no prefetch) inside two weeks and staged (prefetch + batching) in the following 1.5 weeks. Canary for 4-bit would require additional eval time (2–3 weeks).

Monica
Implementation Program Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@nimbus.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-26T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: cost/perf decisions we need for POC

Thanks all — quick answers:

- Concurrency: live-support ~40 RPS at peak (short bursts), async bulk ~120 RPS but can be queued overnight.
- Session key: yes, we have a stable session_id header to enable sticky routing.
- We can ship a 2k labelled sample set by next Monday (6/30) for the 4-bit blind eval.

Samantha — action items noted. Looking forward to the MAP and the cost deltas.

Best,
Samantha Ruiz
Head of ML Ops, NimbusAI
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan-nimbus.docx]
